courseTraceability.rationale: Foundation of Life, Health & Biomedicine Introduces the molecular and cellular foundations of life and biomedical science. Students study biological molecules, cells and membranes, communication, enzymes and energy metabolism, cell division, DNA and heredity, gene expression, genomes and biotechnology. Scientific experiments and papers are analyzed through short teaching contributions and a research-based mini-symposium. A responsive final component selects additional life- and biomedical-science topics with the class.. It implements the explicit academic basis “Human biological function, cellular mechanisms and disease” and “Clinical-problem reasoning, patient context and medical evidence” and “How do biological mechanisms and evidence help explain patient problems?”.

courseTraceability.rationale: Introduction to Brain & Behavior Introduces psychological and neuroscientific explanations of behaviour and mental processes. Students study neural signalling, brain anatomy and development, learning, intelligence, personality, social influence, mental disorders and treatments. Several sessions introduce behavioural, imaging and electrophysiological approaches to neuroscience and their combined use. Interdisciplinary research-article and case analysis connects psychological processes to neural mechanisms and clinical questions.. It implements the explicit academic basis “Human biological function, cellular mechanisms and disease” and “Clinical-problem reasoning, patient context and medical evidence” and “How do biological mechanisms and evidence help explain patient problems?”.

courseTraceability.rationale: Epidemiology & Public Health Introduces epidemiological reasoning and its application to public health. Students measure and interpret disease patterns, study research designs, association, bias, confounding and causality, then examine health determinants, promotion, needs assessment and screening. A local project analyzes a Zeeland health challenge, compares population data, considers affected groups and interventions, and incorporates stakeholder perspectives into feasible recommendations.. It implements the explicit academic basis “Human biological function, cellular mechanisms and disease” and “Clinical-problem reasoning, patient context and medical evidence” and “How do biological mechanisms and evidence help explain patient problems?”.

courseTraceability.rationale: Molecular Cell Biology Studies the molecular mechanisms underlying cellular structure, physiology and regulation, primarily in eukaryotes. Bioenergetics, proteins and membranes connect to genome replication, repair and gene expression, followed by trafficking, signalling, division, tissues, stem cells and cancer. Students evaluate research methods and reproducibility and investigate a drug's molecular target, therapeutic action, metabolism and adverse effects through primary literature, a paper and a research poster.. It implements the explicit academic basis “Human biological function, cellular mechanisms and disease” and “Clinical-problem reasoning, patient context and medical evidence” and “How do biological mechanisms and evidence help explain patient problems?”.

courseTraceability.rationale: Functional Anatomy Studies human anatomical structure in relation to function through regional and body-system blocks. Skeletal, thoracic, cardiovascular, respiratory, abdominal, reproductive and lower urinary anatomy are developed through spatial reasoning, medical images, anatomical drawing and human-specimen material. Guided practicals and dissection-room observation connect three-dimensional relationships to variation. Historical, ethical and societal questions about human remains, representation and sex accompany the anatomical study; activities are framed as academic learning rather than clinical qualification.. It implements the explicit academic basis “Human biological function, cellular mechanisms and disease” and “Clinical-problem reasoning, patient context and medical evidence” and “How do biological mechanisms and evidence help explain patient problems?”.

courseTraceability.rationale: Neurobiology Studies nervous systems and behaviour from comparative, evolutionary and physiological perspectives. Brain anatomy and laboratory introductions support analysis of animal behaviour, research models and welfare. The second part connects regulatory behaviour and biological rhythms to sleep, lifestyle drugs, mood and eating disorders. Comparative-anatomy work and a literature-based disorder report apply neurobiological concepts while animal-research assignments examine reduction, refinement and replacement.. It implements the explicit academic basis “Human biological function, cellular mechanisms and disease” and “Clinical-problem reasoning, patient context and medical evidence” and “How do biological mechanisms and evidence help explain patient problems?”.

courseTraceability.rationale: Research Methods & Statistics Introduces empirical research design and statistical analysis, followed by a substantial student research project. Students study operationalization, measurement quality, sampling, surveys and experimental and nonexperimental designs, then descriptive statistics, estimation, hypothesis testing and introductory regression. R and R Commander support data display and analysis. Project teams develop instruments and a research plan, collect and analyze data, and report results under explicit research-ethics and privacy requirements.. It implements the explicit academic basis “Scientific inquiry, empirical methods and critical evidence appraisal” and “How do biological mechanisms and evidence help explain patient problems?”.

courseTraceability.rationale: Human Physiology Studies normal function and regulation in the adult human body, linking molecular and cellular processes to integrated organ systems. Homeostasis, signalling and energy handling frame nervous, endocrine, muscular, respiratory, cardiovascular, renal, digestive and reproductive functions. Medical examples illustrate physiological principles. An individual literature-based paper examines a selected physiological or pathophysiological process and is developed through structured peer review and revision.. It implements the explicit academic basis “Human biological function, cellular mechanisms and disease” and “Clinical-problem reasoning, patient context and medical evidence” and “How do biological mechanisms and evidence help explain patient problems?”.

courseTraceability.rationale: Biochemistry Examines the chemistry of life, emphasizing biomolecular structure and function, enzymes and metabolic pathways. Students study proteins, carbohydrates, lipids, enzyme kinetics and regulation, glycolysis, gluconeogenesis, the citric-acid cycle, oxidative phosphorylation and further carbohydrate, lipid and nitrogen metabolism. Protein-biochemistry techniques are discussed. A literature-based disease project links a biochemical defect to symptoms, diagnostics and treatment, keeping the molecular mechanism central.. It implements the explicit academic basis “Human biological function, cellular mechanisms and disease” and “Clinical-problem reasoning, patient context and medical evidence” and “How do biological mechanisms and evidence help explain patient problems?”.

R, primarily through R Commander, supports repeated practical exercises; SPSS is an optional alternative. Data-analysis papers and a poster connect research questions and hypotheses to appropriate models, assumption checks, substantive interpretation and APA reporting.. courseTraceability.rationale: Ethics Studies moral reasoning through historical and contemporary ethical theories and close philosophical reading. Utilitarianism, consequentialism, Kantian ethics, virtue ethics, contractarianism and feminist ethics lead into Nietzsche's genealogy, Murdoch's account of goodness and Nagel's treatments of value, perspective, death and meaning. Reflection and research essays require interpretation, argument evaluation and an independent position on ethical theory or a practical ethical problem.. Applications emphasize nervous-system drugs, antimicrobial treatment and inflammatory, immune and airway conditions. Quantitative exercises and virtual experiments model drug responses, while a psychoactive-drug project proposes a testable follow-up experiment.. comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both study molecular and cellular mechanisms and connect them to disease and intervention. UCR develops cell regulation, molecular drug mechanisms and research appraisal; the exact integrated medical cases differ.

Both relate human anatomical structure to function using spatial reasoning and medical images. UCR includes specimens and surface anatomy; the full medical histology, embryology and patient-demonstration integration is not reproduced.

Both study nervous-system anatomy, physiology and dysfunction. UCR uses comparative neurobiology, behavior and disorder research; the dedicated medical neuroanatomy, imaging and clinical examination context remains different.

Both examine integrated organ function, homeostasis and physiological regulation, including cardiovascular, respiratory and renal systems. UCR is a wider physiology course; the medical block and its clinical examples have a different organization.

Both connect biochemical processes and metabolic regulation to health and disease. UCR emphasizes pathways, enzymes and biochemical disease mechanisms; Leiden adds a dedicated endocrine, reproductive and nutritional clinical sequence.

Both analyze infection, immune responses, inflammation and immunopathology in clinical and mechanistic contexts. UCR adds flow-cytometry analysis and research synthesis; the full medical diagnostic and treatment sequence differs.

Both examine cellular and genetic pathology, neoplasia and disease mechanisms. UCR develops molecular diagnosis, genetic ethics and research proposals; the detailed tumor-treatment and hemodynamic case sequence is not identical.

Both study drug targets, pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetics with quantitative reasoning. UCR uses response models, virtual experiments and research design; this does not confer clinical prescribing or reproduce every patient-specific calculation.

Both use organ-system mechanisms and diagnostic findings to reason through cardiovascular, respiratory and renal clinical cases. UCR works with published cases across several systems; it does not reproduce the dedicated patient-based thorax and kidney block.

Both address prevention and health promotion using evidence and patient or population contexts. UCR adds epidemiological designs and a local health project; the package’s specific medical-law and professional-ethics teaching is not replaced.

Both develop research questions, study designs, data analysis and scientific reporting. UCR uses actual empirical projects and R; Leiden integrates research with care-placement data and medical academic formation.

Both develop research-design knowledge, statistical analysis and evidence appraisal. UCR supplies applied multivariable and experimental methods; the full clinical-research package and its medical integration remain different.

Both address patient perspectives, health behavior, medical consultation and communication. UCR includes interviewing practice and health-case formulation; it does not supply BLS, physician physical examination, supervised care or longitudinal medical-skills certification.

Both develop introductory clinical interviewing, assessment and reflective skills. UCR focuses on psychological assessment and psychotherapy; physician consultation, physical examination and the medical portfolio and skills tests remain distinct.
Medicine-specific orientation includes competencies, study preparation and patient perspectives. The UCR program has its own academic introduction and PPD; these are not the same requirement.
A compulsory 3-EC supervised care placement with dependent patients. UCR laboratory, clinical-case and interviewing courses do not reproduce this patient-care experience or assessment.
An integrated adaptive medical-knowledge progress examination with reflection in a portfolio. The UCR program uses course assessments instead.
A credited package including healthcare orientation and AI/technology themes. UCR evidence and health study offers context, but no dedicated equivalent package is assumed.

Healthcare orientation and population-health measurement, including exploration of medical fields. UCR public-health study supplies relevant methods; the required medical orientation is not reproduced.
The current catalogue confirms the 2-EC title and allocation, but supplies no detailed description. Its specific content and correspondence remain unverified.

The dedicated abdominal block integrates differential diagnosis, treatment plans, prosection, imaging and patient demonstrations. UCR has relevant anatomy and disease-case reasoning, but not this complete clinical teaching arrangement.
A further integrated medical-knowledge progress examination, with its own assessment and reflection requirements.

The dedicated locomotion block requires clinical reasoning from history, physical findings and examination across orthopedic, rheumatic and neurological problems. UCR does not reproduce this integrated clinical block.

audience.programmeDescription: Leiden Medicine combines the biological basis of health and disease with clinical problems, patient communication, physical examination, scientific inquiry and professional development. Supervised care experience and longitudinal skills teaching connect medical knowledge with patient care.
audience.comparisonExplanation: This qualified academic-core comparison assesses the documented first 120 EC. UCR can combine substantive biomedical mechanisms and disease-case reasoning with patient perspectives, psychological interviewing and evidence-based inquiry. It does not reproduce physician physical examination, BLS, supervised care placements or longitudinal medical-skills assessment, including those already required in the first two years. All third-year study and final work are outside the comparison; this is not equivalent medical training.

cellNotes.text: Both study molecular and cellular mechanisms and connect them to disease and intervention. UCR develops cell regulation, molecular drug mechanisms and research appraisal; the exact integrated medical cases differ.

Both relate human anatomical structure to function using spatial reasoning and medical images. UCR includes specimens and surface anatomy; the full medical histology, embryology and patient-demonstration integration is not reproduced.

Both examine integrated organ function, homeostasis and physiological regulation, including cardiovascular, respiratory and renal systems. UCR is a wider physiology course; the medical block and its clinical examples have a different organization.

Both connect biochemical processes and metabolic regulation to health and disease. UCR emphasizes pathways, enzymes and biochemical disease mechanisms; Leiden adds a dedicated endocrine, reproductive and nutritional clinical sequence.

Both study nervous-system anatomy, physiology and dysfunction. UCR uses comparative neurobiology, behavior and disorder research; the dedicated medical neuroanatomy, imaging and clinical examination context remains different.

Both analyze infection, immune responses, inflammation and immunopathology in clinical and mechanistic contexts. UCR adds flow-cytometry analysis and research synthesis; the full medical diagnostic and treatment sequence differs.

Both examine cellular and genetic pathology, neoplasia and disease mechanisms. UCR develops molecular diagnosis, genetic ethics and research proposals; the detailed tumor-treatment and hemodynamic case sequence is not identical.

Both study drug targets, pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetics with quantitative reasoning. UCR uses response models, virtual experiments and research design; this does not confer clinical prescribing or reproduce every patient-specific calculation.

Both use organ-system mechanisms and diagnostic findings to reason through cardiovascular, respiratory and renal clinical cases. UCR works with published cases across several systems; it does not reproduce the dedicated patient-based thorax and kidney block.

Both develop research questions, study designs, data analysis and scientific reporting. UCR uses actual empirical projects and R; Leiden integrates research with care-placement data and medical academic formation.

Both develop research-design knowledge, statistical analysis and evidence appraisal. UCR supplies applied multivariable and experimental methods; the full clinical-research package and its medical integration remain different.

Both address patient perspectives, health behavior, medical consultation and communication. UCR includes interviewing practice and health-case formulation; it does not supply BLS, physician physical examination, supervised care or longitudinal medical-skills certification.

Both develop introductory clinical interviewing, assessment and reflective skills. UCR focuses on psychological assessment and psychotherapy; physician consultation, physical examination and the medical portfolio and skills tests remain distinct.

Both address prevention and health promotion using evidence and patient or population contexts. UCR adds epidemiological designs and a local health project; the package’s specific medical-law and professional-ethics teaching is not replaced.
